summary: GPipe is a pipeline-parallelism library (under Lingvo) that takes a model as a sequence of layers with optional per-layer cost estimates, partitions consecutive layers into K cells placed on K accelerators, splits each mini-batch into M micro-batches pipelined through the cells, and applies one synchronous gradient update per mini-batch. Re-materialization at partition boundaries cuts activation memory, and only activation tensors cross device boundaries.
why_read: The manual, sequence-of-layers pipeline-parallel baseline that later compilers (GSPMD pipelining, Alpa inter-operator pass) subsume or automate; also the source of the micro-batch bubble bound O((K-1)/(M+K-1)).
main_contribution: Synchronous micro-batch pipeline parallelism with re-materialization, giving near-linear training throughput with accelerator count for balanced layer stacks and gradient updates independent of the partition count.
main_limitation: Each layer must fit one accelerator; the cost-balancing partitioner is an unspecified heuristic that leaves load imbalance on networks like AmoebaNet; layers that need cross-batch statistics complicate micro-batching.
evaluation_method: Maximum trainable model size and normalized training throughput versus partition count K and micro-batch count M on Cloud TPUv2/v3 and on P100 GPUs without NVLink; two end-to-end training studies (ImageNet, 103-language NMT). No other model-parallel system is measured.
benchmarks: AmoebaNet-D / AmoebaNet-B image classification (ImageNet 2012, transfer to CIFAR, Cars, Pets, Food-101, Aircraft, Birdsnap)
Transformer (24- to 128-layer, up to 83.9B parameters) multilingual NMT on 102 languages to English
states_relationship_to: Chen et al. 2016, sublinear memory cost [14]
Model parallelism / device placement: Krizhevsky [42], Lee et al. [43], Mirhoseini et al. [44], Dean et al. DistBelief [45]
notes: Catalog title is the v1 title; the v5 text read is titled 'GPipe: Easy Scaling with Micro-Batch Pipeline Parallelism'. Table 1 labels the AmoebaNet row 'NVIDIA GPUs (8GB each)' while Sec. 3 says Cloud TPUv2 (8GB); unresolved. ir_representation and compiler_architecture left empty: the paper describes a library over Lingvo with no IR or compiler. 'analytic-optimization' rests only on the statement that the partitioner minimizes variance of estimated cell costs; the algorithm itself is not given. 'communication-pipelining' reflects per-micro-batch activation transfers at boundaries (Sec. 2.2, Sec. 6).
